# CONSUME

> A memecoin on NEAR that eats other memecoins. Feed it a listed memecoin and you get a Bond, an NFT that releases $CONSUME over 30 days. Every $CONSUME can be burned for its share of every memecoin in the Stomach.

This file is for AI agents. Everything below can be checked against the contract itself.

CONSUME is an entry in NEAR HACKATHON (https://nearhackathon.com), in the Memecoins With Mechanics track.

## Connect

- MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no key, no sign-in): `https://consume.cash/api/mcp`
- MCP server (stdio), from the repository: `node agents/mcp.mjs`
- The server reads the chain and prepares unsigned calls. It holds no key and signs nothing. Your own wallet signs.

Tools: `overview`, `list_memecoins`, `feast_race`, `quote_feeding`, `quote_redeem`, `account`, `bond`, `recent_feedings`, `ledger`, `prepare_feed`, `prepare_collect`, `prepare_break_seal`, `prepare_redeem`, `prepare_test_deposit`. Call `overview` first.

## Where it runs

- Network: NEAR testnet
- CONSUME contract: `consume.consumecash.testnet`
- NEAR Intents stand-in (testnet only, simulates deposits from other chains): `intents.consumecash.testnet`
- RPC: `https://test.rpc.fastnear.com`

## The rules, as the contract holds them

- It eats ten memecoins: DOGE, SHIB, PEPE, PENGU, SPX, TURBO, BOME, BLACKDRAGON, SHITZU, NearKat. Fed memecoins go into the Stomach and stay there until someone redeems.
- A feeding earns $CONSUME at the backing: the Stomach's value divided by all $CONSUME, locked or not. So a feeding never dilutes a holder.
- The tithe is the part of a feeding that earns no $CONSUME and so goes to everyone already holding. It starts at 1% and steps up 1% for every $10,000 fed, to 10% at most.
- A Bond releases its $CONSUME evenly over 30 days. Collect what has been released at any time.
- Break the seal to leave early: you receive what has been released plus half of what is still locked. The other half is never minted.
- Redeem burns $CONSUME and pays the same share of every memecoin in the Stomach.
- The Feast: each week the most fed memecoin (by USD) wins. For the following week, feeding it pays no tithe.
- Limits: each memecoin has a largest feeding and a daily cap in USD (`list_memecoins`). The caps are per memecoin, not per account, so splitting a feeding across accounts gains nothing.
- Prices are posted by the Assayer from NEAR Intents quotes. A feeding is refused when a price is older than 15 minutes. Redeeming needs no price and stays open.
- There is no owner and no method that changes a number. A guardian can seal or unseal a listed memecoin and replace the Assayer, nothing else, and the role can be renounced. On testnet the contract account still holds its deployment key; the repository's README says when that changes.

## Reading the contract directly

View methods, all free: `get_config`, `get_stats`, `get_tribes`, `get_epoch_fed`, `quote_meal`, `quote_redeem`, `get_vest`, `get_vests_for_owner`, `get_recent_vests`, `get_meal_credit`, `get_owed`, plus the NEP-141 and NEP-171 standards. Dollar amounts are in millionths of a dollar. $CONSUME has 18 decimals.

## The log of every mint and burn

- `ledger` (or `https://consume.cash/api/ledger` as JSON) lists every feeding, every $CONSUME minted and every $CONSUME burned, newest first, each with its transaction. On a busy contract the oldest entries can drop off the list; the totals are the contract's own and stay right.
- A feeding mints nothing: it writes $CONSUME into a Bond. $CONSUME is minted by `claim` and `exit`, and burned by `redeem`.
- The entries are parsed from the contract's own events (`meal`, `claim`, `exit`, `redeem`). The tool says whether they add up to the totals in `get_stats`.

## Acting

- Feed: `mt_transfer_call` on the NEAR Intents contract with `receiver_id` set to the CONSUME contract. `prepare_feed` builds it, with the slippage floor and deadline the site uses.
- Collect: `claim`. Break the seal: `exit` (1 yoctoNEAR). Redeem: `redeem` (1 yoctoNEAR).
- On testnet, `prepare_test_deposit` gives free test memecoins, once an hour per memecoin.

## More

- Site: https://consume.cash
- Bots that use these calls (dry run unless told to sign): `agents/bots.mjs` in the repository
- A 60 day simulation of supply and backing under four scenarios: `sim/` in the repository
